verified_metadata.title: Certified Monotonic Neural Networks
verified_metadata.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33

metadata_sources.supports: Official title, ordered four-author list, NeurIPS 2020 volume 33, and method abstract.
Official BibTeX confirms ordered authors, pages 15427--15438, volume 33, publisher and year.

artifact.version_note: Official NeurIPS 2020 proceedings PDF. First-page title and ordered four-author list match the official proceedings.

contexts.evidence: Abstract and Section 1, pp. 1--2: the paper certifies monotonicity using MILP after gradient regularization, explicitly avoiding hand-designed weight-space constraints. It belongs in a history of structured monotone models, but not specifically sign-constrained architectures.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The use of monotonicity and convexity to structure interpretable models runs from monotonic networks \parencite{Sill1997_MonotonicNetworks,Daniels2010_MonotoneNN} through certified and lattice-based monotone models \parencite{Liu2020CertifiedMonotone,Gupta2016MonotoneLattice,Sivaraman2020_COMET,Nguyen2023_MonoNet,Runje_2023} to \acp{icnn} \parencite{Amos2017} and convex network calculus \parencite{Bach2017ConvexNN,Calafiore2019DLSE,sivaprasad2021curious}.

contexts.evidence: Abstract and Section 1, pp. 1--2: their method uses heuristic monotonicity regularization with MILP certification of arbitrary piecewise-linear networks, expressly without imposed weight-sign constraints.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Weight-sign constraints are an established device for building monotone models \parencite{Sill1997_MonotonicNetworks,Daniels2010_MonotoneNN} and remain central to modern monotone architectures \parencite{Runje_2023}; monotonicity can also be certified without imposing such constraints \parencite{Liu2020CertifiedMonotone}.

contexts.evidence: Section 1, p. 2, contrasts restrictive hand-designed monotone architectures with certification and specifically notes that nonnegative-weight ReLU networks form a restricted convex subclass. The thesis-specific accuracy results are not attributed to this source.

notes: Current entry names Xiyang Liu and Samuel Coogan; neither is an author of this paper. The existing PDF URL identifies the correct paper despite the wrong author list.
No DOI is supplied by the official proceedings record.

verified_metadata.title: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality with Convex Neural Networks

metadata_sources.supports: Official JMLR title, author, article number, year and page range.

artifact.version_note: Official JMLR article, volume 18(19), pp. 1–53; first page confirms April 2017 publication and sole author.

contexts.evidence: The abstract and §§2.1–2.2 develop convex optimization over infinite-width networks; §4.2, p. 18, splits a signed measure into positive and negative measures, giving a difference of positively homogeneous convex functions. This supports the broad convex-network-calculus reference, subject to the scope note.

notes: Scope clarification: “convex neural networks” here primarily means a convex infinite-dimensional optimization formulation; the represented functions need not be input-convex or monotone. §4.2 nevertheless explicitly gives a signed-measure DC decomposition.
